name: @longtermsupport/ts-qa-ci
description: Orchestrated QA/CI pipeline for TypeScript/React projects - the TS analogue of lts/php-qa-ci
_peerDependenciesPolicy: Floors are set to the CURRENT major generation as of the last version check (npm view <pkg> version), not an old baseline carried forward out of habit — ts-qa-ci should push consumers toward current stable tooling, not accommodate years-old installs. Re-run `npm view <pkg> version` for every peerDependency before each ts-qa-ci release and bump these floors to the then-current major; do not silently let them go stale. EXCEPTIONS (both found 2026-07-10 while dogfooding on lts-commerce-site, Plan 011 Task 4.1 — verify `npm view <plugin> peerDependencies` for the key ecosystem plugin, not just the tool's own version, before raising either floor again): (1) typescript is capped below its own latest major because typescript-eslint 8.63.0 (latest, and its canary) still caps at `typescript >=4.8.4 <6.1.0` even though TypeScript 7.x has shipped stable — floor set to 6.0.3, the newest version actually inside that ceiling. (2) eslint is capped below its own latest major because eslint-plugin-react 7.37.5 (latest, last published 2025-04-03, no `next` tag support for it either) still caps at `eslint ^3...^9.7` — using ESLint 10 would break every consumer running eslint-plugin-react (i.e. effectively every React consumer). Floor set to 9.39.4, the newest 9.x release.

knownGaps: Toolchain 4.1 and 4.4: the dependency-cruiser lane has no single-rule harness and ignores -p, so the bundled no-circular defence cannot be run alone or over a subset (detector specification 4.2 and 5.2).

Toolchain 4.2: ts-qa rule-doc resolves ts-qa/ identifiers only; the bundled dependency-cruiser defence no-circular is unknown to it and the Tier A core rule no-restricted-syntax resolves to an upstream URL rather than to the shipped as/enum ban documentation.
Toolchain 4.3: ESLint reads an eslint-suppressions.json file from the project root and a finding it lists is silenced; nothing disables the file or fails on its presence.
Toolchain 5.1 and 5.3: ts-qa rules is derived from the resolved ESLint configuration only, so the bundled dependency-cruiser defence no-circular is absent from the listing.
Toolchain 8.1: the release self-audit covers ts-qa/ identifiers only; no-circular is outside it.
Toolchain 8.2: ts-qa/no-naive-datetime-template is declared Tier A but the shipped generic configuration never enables it, so it runs neither on this package nor in a consuming project.
Method 3.3: ts-qa/no-duplicate-section-ids and ts-qa/no-placeholder have no fixture test proving they fire.
Toolchain 4.3: the eslint-suppressions.json route is open on this repository's own tooling as it is for consumers.
Toolchain 5.1: this repository's dependency-cruiser defence no-circular is absent from ts-qa rules.
